The air was thick with the scent of wet earth and the distant, sharp tang of lightning as the storm rolled in, dark clouds churning overhead like a restless sea. Eva stood beneath the sprawling oak, its gnarled branches reaching out like skeletal fingers, a refuge from the rain that would soon drench the landscape. She tugged her jacket tighter around her shoulders, feeling the fabric cling to her skin, dampening with the rising humidity. Each breath she took filled her lungs with the raw, electric promise of the coming downpour.

A rustle in the underbrush caught her attention, and she turned, heart quickening, half-expecting a deer or perhaps a wayward fox. Instead, it was just a cluster of leaves swaying in the wind, and she exhaled, a nervous laugh escaping her lips. “Get it together, Eva,” she murmured under her breath, her voice barely louder than the whisper of the breeze. The solitude was beginning to gnaw at her, every rustling leaf a reminder of the weight of her own isolation.

Then came the first fat drops of rain, splattering against the ground with a soft plop that echoed in the quiet. She tilted her head back, allowing the cool moisture to kiss her skin, feeling it mingle with the heat of her anxiety. It was a fleeting moment of comfort, yet another reminder of her own vulnerability. “Just a little rain,” she told herself, but her thoughts raced ahead, spiraling into what lay beyond the storm—confrontations waiting to unfold, words left unsaid that hung in the air like the thickening clouds.
